builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: AutoBuddy: Evaluating Proactive, Always-On Agents on Task Discovery and Execution in a Simulated Workplace
summary: AutoBuddy-Bench replaces task-given agent benchmarks with a simulated organisation rendered as workspace artefacts, in which the agent must both discover obligations and execute them, with outcomes computed from world state rather than reference answers. It costs nothing to deploy at inference but adopting its methodology requires building or running the full simulator, and its reference agent pattern (discovery pass with source grounding, then isolated execution sessions with write access) is the only directly reusable design element. The reported failure pattern can mislead if overgeneralised: weaker models fail at discovery, intermediate models stop short of execution, and strong models fail on business-system operations, but these findings are tied to the specific backbones and simulated systems tested and may not transfer to a given production stack.
rationale: The paper contributes an evaluation environment and diagnostic finding rather than a deployable technique, so it informs how the reader should test always-on agents but requires no production adoption.
technique: Simulated-workplace benchmark for proactive agent evaluation
